analysis.title: International Market Intelligence Morning Briefing (October 30, 2026)
key_insights: Tech earnings released after the close on Oct 29 met steep price declines, while defensives were bid in Asia. Oct 30 is the last trading day of what the desk calls an unpleasant month.
The desk sees a resumption of combat operations in the Middle East as the consensus baseline. It says that could mean risk/reward on crude is very negative.
Policy continuity is the most likely outcome after Lagarde departs.
Wednesday and Thursday earnings were not obviously negative for AI infrastructure, but they challenged the tactical bounce the desk expected. The next clearing event could be the midterms.

The broadening trade (SXXP, UKX, SPW and SPX ex AI made new highs on Oct 29) has so far been a reliable hedge against AI exposure. The desk calls much of this mechanical or positioning-driven and notes 50% of SPX stocks have a negative beta to the index.

Halfway through the season, earnings growth is better than consensus. Europe's growth is above the US on both median and index-level bases, and US ex-Mag7 growth is above Mag7. Fewer companies are beating estimates than last quarter and input cost pressure is intensifying.
Bullion is still not hedging portfolios after the largest crypto hack on record. If $4000 gold breaks, $3500/$3600 could be the next support.
APAC clients are more bearish than US clients and less bearish than EU clients. They are still up double digits on the year, so many lack incentive to re-engage until a clear trend emerges.

The desk argues the US consumer is robust. The top 4 income quintiles hold 6% to 27% more inflation-adjusted cash than at YE2019, nearly $8T in nominal terms. Retail sales are running at $723bn a month versus $505bn in 2019, and card delinquencies are normalizing to pre-COVID trends rather than deteriorating.

Consumer sub-sectors differ. Airlines, cruise and hotels show robust demand. Autos and homebuilders are rate-sensitive, so the desk suggests parts and suppliers. Retailers face freight costs that clients put at 30-40% of total cost, with rates more than tripled YTD. Staples are most at risk of margin compression and likely remain a source of funds.

Credit markets are becoming more discriminating on AI infrastructure, but the desk sees no broader funding crisis. AI infrastructure has absorbed more than $500 billion of debt YTD. Leveraged GPU and data center developers face tighter financing while hyperscalers are well positioned.

AI-related CDS spreads have widened mostly on technical selling and hedging demand, since banks are buying protection against data center lending exposure. CDS now trades above comparable cash-bond spreads, which the desk says creates opportunity for investors willing to sell protection.

The desk calls CRWV a financing challenge, not a solvency one. JPM credit analyst Tom Egan projects last-12-month EBITDA rising from about $4.4b in June 2026 to $7.3b by YE and nearly $20b by YE27, backed by about $130b of contracted revenue.

ORCL and SpaceX credit spreads widened significantly on reports each is seeking off-balance-sheet financing. Erica Spear expects hyperscalers to keep investing but says growing debt supply may pressure credit spreads into 2027.

The desk says concerns that France leads EU-wide distress are exaggerated. It sees a French idiosyncratic story, not a sovereign crisis 2.0, and notes the ECB backstop (TPI, OMT, PEPP flexibility), although activation is conditional.

French OATs discount debt/GDP above 150% versus about 120% actual and an implied deficit above 8% versus about 5% debated. The desk makes no call for a material reversal before the 2Q27 elections but sees room for relief into year-end around the budget discussion.

EU Banks are trading like the 2011-12 sovereign crisis, but the desk says the earnings trend is unchanged and dips of more than 15% versus the index should be bought. It sees call ratio spreads and call spreads as attractive.

On the midterms, the desk says federal AI regulation is unlikely because a veto override needs a 2/3 majority in both chambers. If Democrats take the House they could defund Middle East military efforts. Tariff policy is unlikely to change, and longer-dated bonds could see a bid if deficit spending is halted.

On Treasuries, the pre-Oct 22 view was that a 5.50% 10-year yield was more likely than 5.00%. The market prices a hike in Dec 2026 and two in FY27. Clients see upside risk to that pricing, and the downside risk is a near-term end to the US/Iran conflict with oil normalizing.

Client pushback on AI/tech: semis revenue relies on supply-constraint price spikes that are unsustainable in a DCF, neocloud turmoil may spread to the whole group, and software is unlikely to be a source of funds. A buy needs a positioning flush, hyperscaler capex confirmation, semis earnings, tighter credit and positive seasonality, pointing to early November.

Since the July 28 local lows SPX is +4.8% through Oct 22, but over half the index has a negative return and 69% of stocks lag the SPX. This makes picking a single stock and hedging with a sector ETF difficult.

The desk says AI and ex-AI can work together short term but not longer term. Revenue and earnings differentials point to tech dominance once the market stabilizes. About 65% of SPX companies cited AI operating improvement in 26Q2 earnings but fewer than 5% quantified it.

Client funding-short ideas are a combination of Consumer, Healthcare, smidcaps and Europe to offset tech exposure. Aero/Def has a negative client outlook on the risk of a Blue Wave halting military funding, with a lame-duck defense funding bill as an upside surprise.

Other asset classes: clients see the dollar range-bound and likely at a local high, gold as trading inversely to the dollar despite central bank demand, and none view credit as superior to equities. They agree with the JPM copper bull case tied to a China growth reboot, and see silver as part of the AI trade.

The desk is tactically bullish on global equities, preferring long US and Asia (Japan, Korea, Taiwan) versus EU. It sees the US as overheating, Europe recovering from stagflation, and wants stability in EGB spreads before broadening gains conviction in EU.

Longs: infrastructure (inference, semi cap), less-levered hyperscalers, AI-vulnerable software, EU and JA banks, EU industrials, JA machinery, GE Infra, EU miners, EU Pharma and UKX, and selective consumer. Shorts: AI-vulnerable ex-software, short-cycle data center capex names, EU insurance, autos, chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, MedTech and MDAX.
EM is bullish on global macro strength, AI capex tailwinds and broadening exposure via commodities. EM has recovered over 9% of its drawdown since end-July. The desk favors country-relative trades.
Hedge funds are -3.3% MTD globally versus SPX +0.2%, so the pain came from moves under the surface. Eq L/S 20d alpha is the worst since Feb '21 and Multi-Strat alpha the worst since Aug '24.

CTAs were the steadiest sellers, with US equity exposure down every day since 10/13 led by Nasdaq. HF net flows were only -0.9z, multi-strat de-grossing slowed sharply, quants kept adding gross and retail stayed net buyers at the slowest pace in a year. The desk reads this as systematic de-risking, not a large liquidation event.

Combined ETF, retail and HF 60d relative flows into Info Tech are near record highs at +3z. Utilities, Real Estate and Materials are at or near extreme low flows, and Healthcare is the defensive exception.

Positioning has not fully cleared. Eq L/S net leverage is at 12m and 3yr lows but gross leverage is still above average. Risks are continued alpha deterioration, CTAs that could still sell given neutral positioning, and soft retail demand.

market_movers.rationale: JPM HY credit analyst Tom Egan calls it a financing challenge, not a solvency one, with EBITDA projected near $20b by YE27. The desk flags its CDS at a slightly positive basis with converts outstanding as interesting.
Credit spreads widened significantly on reports it is seeking off-balance-sheet financing, and more externally financed names have underperformed.

sector_views.rationale: Tactically bullish on inference and long-cycle infrastructure such as semi cap and on less-levered hyperscalers. Earnings challenged the near-term bounce, and the desk wants a positioning flush and capex confirmation.
Clients see it as unlikely to be a source of funds, with security and infrastructure software as consensus longs. The desk also lists AI-vulnerable application software among longs.
Earnings trend is unchanged and dips of more than 15% versus the index should be bought.
Viewed by clients as most at risk of margin compression and a likely source of funds with higher rates and inflation.
Clients have a negative outlook given the potential for a Blue Wave to halt a military funding spike, though a lame-duck defense funding bill could surprise to the upside.
Listed as challenged industries among the desk's shorts.
Combined flows are at or near extreme lows (Utilities 60d -2.5z, Real Estate 20d -4.9z, Materials 60d -2.7z).

earnings_insights: Tech earnings released after the close on Oct 29 were all met with steep price declines.
Halfway through the season, earnings growth is coming in better than consensus. Europe's earnings growth is above the US on median and index-level bases, and US ex-Mag7 growth is above Mag7.
Fewer companies are beating estimates than last quarter and input cost pressure is intensifying.
The desk says AMZN is installing an AI accelerator about every 14 seconds, and that Wednesday and Thursday earnings were not obviously negative for AI infrastructure.

Next week 20% of SPX and 17% of SXXP report. Scheduled names include AAPL and PLTR (Nov 2), ANET, APO, ALAB, ISP and RACE (Nov 3), QCOM, ARM, DDOG, APP, NOVOB and BMW (Nov 4), NET, LITE, DBK, RHM, Toyota and Sony (Nov 5), and MRNA (Nov 6).
Retailers face idiosyncratic issues at LULU and NKE on top of freight costs of 30-40% of total cost per client feedback.
About 65% of SPX companies mentioned AI improvement in operations in 26Q2 earnings, but fewer than 5% quantified the impact.

macro_indicators.reading: $723bn per month YTD2026 versus $505bn in 2019 and $420bn in 2014
macro_indicators.interpretation: Spending growth is almost double the pre-COVID rate, and the desk says higher energy prices are not crowding out discretionary spending.
Used as a proxy for non-public business health, which supports the view that the corporate sector is healthy.

macro_indicators.reading: One hike priced in Dec 2026 and two more in FY27
macro_indicators.interpretation: Clients see upside risk to this pricing given household and corporate balance sheets, growth and inflation. Fewer hikes would require a near-term end to the US/Iran conflict and oil normalization.

macro_indicators.reading: No hikes in FY27, cuts in FY28 and FY29, 2% target reached in FY29
macro_indicators.interpretation: Many clients think the dots are not tied to high-probability outcomes, so market pricing remains the baseline for equity investors.

macro_indicators.reading: 5.50% seen as more likely than 5.00% before the Oct 22 rally
macro_indicators.interpretation: The pre-rally JPM view was for higher yields, and the desk notes the 10Y has averaged 3.14% this decade versus 2.39% in the 2010s.

crypto_views: The biggest crypto hack of all time has not helped gold, which still is not hedging portfolios.

trade_ideas.description: Buy EU Banks on dips of more than 15% versus the index, using call ratio spreads and call spreads
trade_ideas.rationale: The earnings trend for EU Banks is unchanged while the tape echoes the 2011-12 sovereign crisis.

trade_ideas.description: Sell CDS protection on AI infrastructure names trading at a positive basis, such as CRWV
trade_ideas.rationale: Bank hedging demand has pushed CDS spreads above comparable cash-bond spreads.
trade_ideas.risk: Near-term credit spreads have been bumpy and growing debt supply may pressure spreads into 2027.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically long China Star 50 versus China Internet (KWEB)
trade_ideas.rationale: Star 50 captures more innovative and AI-exposed names, while large cap internet is more exposed to Chinese consumers.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically long Korea versus South East Asia (ASEA)
trade_ideas.rationale: Expresses the AI winners versus losers view.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically long Taiwan after the global tech selloff in July
trade_ideas.rationale: Taiwan offers a less volatile exposure to AI and Asia tech relative to Korea.
Potential structural policy shift after the second round of the presidential vote. Brazil also diversifies against weakness in the EM AI theme and is relatively resilient to geopolitical risks.

trade_ideas.description: Long EM (EEM) for greater exposure to potential broadening
trade_ideas.rationale: Global macro strength, AI capex tailwinds, commodity-based broadening exposure and scope for policy easing.

trade_ideas.description: Option hedge: keep MCX < UKX, and short France versus EU Domestics
trade_ideas.rationale: Clarity is needed on spending, pragmatism and ideology, and the second leg is a view on French politics and dislocation.

risk_factors: Tech earnings reactions have challenged the tactical bounce in AI infrastructure.
Resumption of combat in the Middle East.
Rising rates and a hike path priced by the market, with clients seeing upside risk to pricing.
Growing AI debt issuance, interconnected and circular financing, and rising borrowing costs.
Concentration and correlated downside risk from Nvidia credit support to GPU customers such as CRWV.
Neocloud turmoil could spread across the group, with bankruptcy risk.
French fiscal concerns and EGB spread widening, with ECB support conditional on activation.
Input cost pressure is intensifying and fewer companies are beating estimates.
Continued Eq L/S alpha deterioration, possible further CTA selling and soft retail demand.
Freight and transportation cost increases for retailers.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge funds are -3.3% MTD globally (from -2.1% last week) versus SPX +0.2% MTD and ACWI -1.0%. YTD HF returns slipped to +4.7% from +6%.
Eq L/S 20d alpha of -2.9% is the worst since Feb '21, Multi-Strat alpha is the worst since Aug '24, and 60d crowding returns of -4.1% are back to July '24 levels.
HF net flows were -0.9z (gross -0.6z). Multi-Strat 5d gross de-grossing slowed to -0.9% from -3.3% a week ago. Quants kept adding gross at the 80th percentile.

CTA US equity exposure has fallen every day since 10/13, led by Nasdaq, and is only around the 45th percentile long term, so CTAs could still sell. Retail net buying is at the 5th percentile over 20 days.
Combined ETF, retail and HF 60d relative flows into Info Tech are near record at +3z versus a +3.4z peak in late Sep.

US TPM is at the 28th percentile, Europe the 8th and China/HK at -2z. Eq L/S net leverage is at 12m and 3yr lows while gross leverage is at the 77th percentile over 12m and 95th over 5yr despite falling 4.4% WoW.
AI Core Revenue and Semis positioning fell to the 94th percentile long term from the 99th.
Hedge ideas: keep MCX < UKX until clarity emerges, and short FR versus EU domestics on politics and dislocation.
Call ratio spreads and call spreads are attractive on EU Banks given the dip-buying view.
The AI-related CDS basis is positive in some names, and the desk likes selling protection where CDS trades above cash spreads, with only initial margin to post.
geopolitical: A resumption of combat operations in the Middle East is now the consensus baseline.
The US/Iran conflict could end near term, which would bring quick normalization of oil, refined product, petrochemical prices and shipping and insurance rates.
If Democrats take the House in the US midterms they could defund military efforts in the Middle East, forcing an off-ramp for Trump.
Tariff policy is unlikely to change after the midterms given the President's latitude over foreign policy.
France faces fiscal concerns and elections in 2Q27, and Exporters are exposed to geopolitics and tariffs.
Brazil's second round of the presidential election takes place at the end of the month.
Lagarde's departure from the ECB, with policy continuity seen as most likely.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings were not obviously negative for AI infrastructure, with AMZN installing an AI accelerator about every 14 seconds, and fundamentals remain positive. ETFs are buying the dip and quants are re-grossing.
tension_points.bear_case: Tech earnings met steep price declines and challenged the tactical bounce. Clients cite unsustainable supply-constrained semis pricing, neocloud turmoil and financing strain.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A buy needs a positioning flush, hyperscaler capex confirmation, semis earnings, tighter credit and positive seasonality, pointing to early November. The desk names the midterms as the next clearing event.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers are fundamentally resilient and the funding ecosystem is functional. Wide CDS reflects hedging demand, which creates a positive basis for protection sellers.
tension_points.bear_case: Growing debt supply, circular financing and higher borrowing costs may pressure spreads into 2027, and leveraged GPU and data center developers face tighter financing.

tension_points.bull_case: Debt/GDP is about 120% against the 180% level the desk treats as a tipping point, OATs discount a deficit above 8% versus about 5% debated, and the ECB backstop limits disorderly widening.
tension_points.bear_case: France has a primary deficit of about 3% and below-potential growth. Crowded hedge fund carry positioning and a non-resident holder base worsened the move.
tension_points.what_invalidates: ECB backstop activation is conditional, and the desk expects no material reversal before elections in 2Q27.

theme_stances.key_argument: Earnings were not obviously negative for AI infrastructure but did not deliver the expected tactical bounce.
theme_stances.evidence: Earnings didn't do the job, so the next clearing event could be the midterms.

theme_stances.key_argument: The desk says concerns that France is a leading indicator of EU-wide distress are exaggerated.
The broadening trade has so far remained a reliable hedge against AI exposure, backed by better earnings growth in Europe and US ex-Mag7.
